title: Minimum, maximum and mean in one pass

blocks.text: `Collectors.teeing(first, second, merger)` (Java 12+) feeds every element to two collectors at once and merges their two results, so one pass over the data yields two views of it. Primitive streams bring their own reductions: `IntStream.average()` returns an `OptionalDouble`.
`OnePass.MinMax` is a record `(int min, int max)`. Write two static methods in `OnePass`:

items: `Optional<MinMax> range(List<Integer> numbers)`: the smallest and largest number, found in one stream pass.
`double mean(List<Integer> numbers)`: the average of the numbers, or `0.0` when there are none.

blocks.text: Both methods may be handed an empty list, or a list with no positive number in it.

cases.says: It finds the minimum, the maximum and the mean of the numbers.
An empty list has no range, so the result is an empty Optional instead of an exception.
The mean of an empty list is 0.0, not NaN from dividing by a zero count.
The range of all-negative numbers has a negative maximum: 0 is no starting value for max.

concepts: Primitive streams reduce directly with sum, average and summaryStatistics.
Collectors.teeing feeds two collectors in one pass and merges their results.
